newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan vice premier on secret visit to Netherlands.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan vice premier on secret visit to Netherlands.

text.p: Taiwan vice premier Hsu Li-teh has left secretly for a visit to the Netherlands, but has no plans to meet Dutch government officials to avoid provoking China, a state-run news agency reported Wednesday.
Foreign minister John Chang told the Central News Agency that Hsu, who left Taiwan on Monday, planned to meet investors on a trip that would be "mostly vacation in nature".
"The foreign ministry was not involved (in arranging the trip), nor did the Dutch government make any arrangements," Chang was quoted by the agency as saying.
The Dutch government has said it is coming under commercial pressure from China because of its support for a U.N. resolution critical of China's human rights record.
The resolution was blocked on April 15 after Beijing ralled strong support to sink it.
To evade a diplomatic embargo imposed by China, Taiwan has engaged in what Taipei calls "pragmatic diplomacy" -- quiet, unofficial visits to countries which recognise Beijing instead of Taipei.
China, a rival of Taiwan since the two split after a civil war in 1949, maintains that the island is a renegade province ineligible for foreign relations.
It has warned other countries against forging ties with Taipei or permitting visits by senior officials from Taiwan.

Hsu's visit followed several discreet foreign trips made by Chang and vice president Lien Chan. Between them, Chang and Lien have visited the Ukraine, Singapore, Malaysia, Belgium, the United Arab Emirates and Jordan in the past two years.
Hsu was expected to return to Taiwan next week, the news agency said.
Only 30 countries currently recognise Taiwan's exiled Republic of China government instead of Beijing's communist government.
The island's biggest ally, South Africa, shocked Taipei in November by announcing that it would switch recognition to Beijing by the end of 1997.
